items.title: Camden County Water District Gets $223K For Drinking Water Upgrades
items.desc: CAMDEN COUNTY, Mo. — Camden County Public Water Supply District No. 5 has received a $223,000 interest-free loan from the Missouri Department of Natural Resources to help plan and design future drinking water system improvements.
items.body: CAMDEN COUNTY, Mo. — Camden County Public Water Supply District No. 5 has received a $223,000 interest-free loan from the Missouri Department of Natural Resources to help plan and design future drinking water system improvements. The funding comes through the department’s Planning and Design Loan Program and will cover early engineering and administrative costs while the district works toward a larger construction funding package. The district estimates the full improvement project will cost about $3 million, with construction expected to begin in 2028. According to DNR, the planning loan carries no interest and has a five-year term. The department estimates that will save local ratepayers about $48,000 in interest compared with other financing options. “Investing in local water infrastructure is not just about improving drinking water systems; it’s about revitalizing communities and ensuring residents have access to abundant, safe drinking water,” said Jake Buxton, director of the Missouri Department of Natural Resources. The larger project could eventually qualify for additional financing through Missouri’s Drinking Water State Revolving Fund, which supports improvements to water treatment plants, distribution systems, water storage, supply facilities, and other drinking water infrastructure. DNR said the Camden County project will be funded wholly or in part with money received from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. More information about Missouri drinking water and wastewater funding programs is available through the Department of Natural Resources’ State Revolving Fund program.

items.title: Preschoolers Steal The Show As Camdenton Breaks Ground On New Early Childhood Center
items.desc: On a cloudy Tuesday afternoon, the Camdenton R-III School District — along with some adorable preschoolers — broke ground on the new Early Childhood Center.
items.body: On a cloudy Tuesday afternoon, the Camdenton R-III School District — along with some adorable preschoolers — broke ground on the new Early Childhood Center. Superintendent Brett Thompson called it a historic day, saying the district was turning more than dirt; it was laying a foundation for its youngest Lakers. The district held a ceremony for the project, with Student Board Advisor Carter Saab leading the Pledge of Allegiance. The new center at Dogwood Elementary will include 12 general classrooms focused on pre-K, with four rooms designed as flexible spaces that could serve other needs. There will also be a large multipurpose room and an administrative area, with space serving as a FEMA shelter for approximately 1,609 occupants. Dr. Keith White, assistant superintendent of finance and operations, was originally working with $2 million in FEMA funding before learning an additional $2 million was available. That allowed the district and SAPP Design to expand the project and address needs at Dogwood, which White described as the district's oldest facility. "When we have an opportunity like this, where we can build something new, that can be a jump start for kids and for the future of this community," White said. "To me, it's a no-brainer." Thompson credited the Board of Education, assistant superintendents, SAPP Design, Toth and Associates, and general contractor DeWitt & Associates, emphasizing the amount of work that goes into a project of this size. John McNabb of SAPP Design said the additional FEMA funding changed the scope of the project. While he enjoys architecture in general, he said school projects carry a different kind of meaning. items.title: Marshfield Community Theatre Presents: Carrie: The Musical This Halloween
items.desc: This Halloween season, the Marshfield Community Theatre is bringing you something old and something new. “We are currently producing Carrie: The Musical, based on the iconic story by Stephen King,” […]
items.body: This Halloween season, the Marshfield Community Theatre is bringing you something old and something new. “We are currently producing Carrie: The Musical, based on the iconic story by Stephen King,” shared an excited Kelby Lorenz, Director of Carrie and Director of Outreach for Marshfield Community Theatre. “We chose this show because it’s October; we are doing it Halloween weekend. It seemed like a really good spooky show, but when I read the script, it tells a really incredible story,” reflected Lorenz. “One of the things that I love about this show and the way that it’s interpreted is that it’s a closed loop-we end where we start. We got to really play with the idea of how long have we been stuck in this loop…and how long have we been trying to stop the destruction.” “It’s a cool concept to play with-around the idea of trauma, how it stays with us…and how traumatic moments can really impact the way we interact with each other,” expressed Lorenz. “It really centers on that theme-what does it cost to be kind?” The cast includes around 16, with most actors new to MCT, including a mix of MSU students and brand-new actors. The production team includes Lorenz as Director, Nico Jenkins as Assistant Director, Linley Wilson as Music Director, Miliani Kloster as Choreographer, and Toni Lorenz as Production Manager. “It’s been super fun,” shared Lauren Knight, a Missouri State student playing Carrie White. “I haven’t done a lot of roles where I’m a lead- it’s been a bit of a change. It’s been fun to get to know this character. She’s been a bit of a challenge…I’ve learned to be more vulnerable on stage.
